title: JALLIANWALA BAGH
subtitle: The Garden the Empire Could Not Bury
posterMeta: 1919 · THE GARDEN · THE ORDER · THE INQUIRY
logline: On 13 April 1919, a walled garden in Amritsar became the place where the British Empire stopped being able to call itself lawful.

style.look: dusk ochre, deep charcoal, aged paper, brass, dust in hard light, restrained typography
rules: Show the object before the explanation: a notice, a wall, a watch, a well.
No bodies, no blood, no reconstructed killing. The aftermath carries the violence.
One idea per shot. The camera pushes, reveals, or holds. It never drifts.
Use silence as a cut. Let the narration stop before the next image lands.
Every number on screen is an official figure or explicitly attributed.

blender.role: procedural sets, wall, gate, well, watch, lamp, memorial, hero stills

node.role: timeline, Chromium camera moves, ffmpeg encode, captions, metadata

youtube.title: Jallianwala Bagh: The Garden the Empire Could Not Bury
youtube.description: A short cinematic history of 13 April 1919: the order, the garden, the firing, the inquiry, and the argument that never ended. Sources below.

scenes.title: The order
scenes.purpose: Open on the paper that made a peaceful gathering illegal.

narration.text: Jallianwala Bagh.
A garden in Amritsar. A banned meeting. A general who decided to teach a city a lesson.
The Rowlatt Act had allowed detention without trial. Punjab was already on edge.

shots.camera: locked title card, a slow 2.5% scale
shots.visual: The film title in bone-white serif on black, with a thin gold rule and a line of small caps. No texture, no noise, no decoration.
A typed notice on a dark desk under a brass lamp: NO PUBLIC MEETINGS. A fountain pen, an inkpot, and a clock at half past four. The paper is the brightest object.

scenes.title: The garden
scenes.purpose: Make the place concrete: a walled garden with one way out.

narration.text: On 13 April 1919, Baisakhi, thousands gathered in the Bagh. Some came to worship. Some came to protest the arrest of two local leaders.
The Bagh was about two hundred yards square, walled to ten feet, with five narrow entrances.
The meeting began at half past five. Dyer arrived an hour later with about fifty soldiers and blocked the main exit.

shots.camera: 38mm, low, slow lateral push toward the gate
shots.visual: A high ochre wall at dusk, patched and weathered, with one round-topped gate. A neem tree leans over the wall. Torn orders cling to the plaster. Late arrivals cross the paving toward the gate; dust hangs in a hard shaft of low sun.

shots.camera: 38mm, low, a slow drift across the gate and its crowd
shots.visual: The gate from outside, close enough that the arch fills the frame. Late arrivals stand as dark silhouettes inside the opening; the wall around them catches the last light. A strip of cloth lies at the threshold.

scenes.title: The firing
scenes.purpose: Turn the order into an event without reconstructing the killing.

narration.text: He gave no warning to disperse. He later said the purpose was not to disperse the meeting, but to punish.
The troops fired into the densest part of the crowd, toward the narrow exits.
The firing lasted about ten minutes. Dyer later reported that his party fired 1,650 rounds.
The official inquiry counted 379 dead. More than 1,200 were wounded. Other estimates were higher.

shots.visual: A brass pocket watch lying in dust. The dial is scratched. The hands stand at 6:30. Dust catches the light along the bezel.
vfx: a slow shadow crossing the face

shots.camera: 55mm, tight on the wall, slow tilt up
shots.visual: The wall in hard side light. Pockmarks, chipped brick and a few embedded rounds across the plaster. A branch throws a living shadow; plaster dust hangs in the air. A stone sill holds three spent cases. No bodies, no blood, no crowd.

shots.camera: 38mm, low, static, the gate slightly off-centre
shots.visual: The gate from outside, now empty. The light has gone amber. A fallen shoe, torn white cloth, dropped paper and three spent cases lie on the paving. Bullet chips freckle the plaster.

scenes.title: The well
scenes.purpose: Let the aftermath be a place, not a statistic.

narration.text: Some died at the gates. Some died in the well.
A plaque at the site says 120 bodies were recovered from the well.
The wounded lay where they fell. Curfew kept help away until morning.
The Empire called it a disturbance. India called it a massacre.

shots.camera: 44mm, high angle, slow descent toward the water
shots.visual: A circular stone well inside the walled garden. The water is black and still; marigold petals and three faint ripples catch the sky. A torn cloth hangs over the rim; a bucket and coiled rope sit beside it. Moss, paving, a lit niche and a tree hold the depth behind.
vfx: a ripple that crosses the water once

shots.camera: 44mm, close on the rim and cloth, static
shots.visual: The stone rim in close-up: wet capstone, moss in the joints, the torn cloth and the dark water just below. Petals drift; the texture of the stone is the only movement.

scenes.title: The inquiry
scenes.purpose: Show what the state did with the truth.

narration.text: The Hunter Commission criticised Dyer. It did not prosecute him.
He was relieved of his command and barred from employment in India.
He was never tried for murder.
Britain has never formally apologised. In 2019 it expressed deep regret.

shots.camera: overhead, locked, a slow lateral drift
shots.visual: A typed report on a dark desk, lit by a brass lamp. Ruled lines, an inkpot, a pen, spectacles, a magnifier and a rubber stamp crowd the frame. The figures 379 and 1,200 are printed in the paper, not added later. A thin red stamp reads NO PROSECUTION.

shots.camera: 55mm, low, slow push toward the flame
shots.visual: A candle in a brass dish on a dark table, a sealed letter, an envelope, a glass, a spent match and a stack of books. A shuttered window holds a cold blue edge. The small flame is the only warm thing in the frame.

scenes.title: The argument
scenes.purpose: Carry the event into the political argument it created.

narration.text: The massacre helped turn the Congress toward mass non-cooperation in 1920 and 1921.
Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest.
The Raj survived the inquiry. It did not survive the loss of trust.
The question is not whether the Empire could kill. It is what a country does with the memory.

shots.camera: 35mm, low, static, the flame small in frame
shots.visual: The candle again, now further away. The letter is open beside a red seal. The window is a cold rectangle; the room is larger and emptier than before.

shots.camera: 42mm, low, slow push into the flame
shots.visual: A bronze plaque in a dark stone hall, gold letters catching a shaft of light. A pierced jali screen glows behind it; marigolds, two small diyas and a brazier hold the foreground. The number 1919 is cut into the plaque. Dust moves through the light.
